events.text: You have sat in front of the gate for a long while, and they walk past you in their black hats, with your own small face on the front. It is a very bad likeness. They say the most remarkable things to each other, at your feet. It has come to you that you have only ever heard people lie in the direction of a stone. You know how the human shape goes on. You wonder what they say when it is only a person listening.

choices.text: Put on the hat. Go down to the drum, and find out

effects.log: One face, your own, with a hat that bears it on top. Nothing could be plainer. You get as far as the first wine-seller, and he tells you that it is a lovely morning, and it is, and you could weep. It is the first true thing you have ever heard in a market.

choices.text: Stay on the plinth. You know what they say

effects.log: You stay. A clerk goes by, telling another clerk that he will certainly speak up for him. It tastes of chinaberry from here. You chew on it, and you are very clean and very tired. There is moss on your left ear.

events.text: Today you stand by the petition drum, and listen. A young man is telling a clerk about his dead uncle's field. It is a very moving story, and it has eleven lies in it, each with its own small sour note. "That is not his field," you say. You had not meant to say anything. All the clerks turn around.

choices.text: Stay, and tell them whose it is

effects.log: It is a widow's, as it turns out. They look into it. She comes by the next week and looks at you for a long time, without thanking you. It seems that she will now have to deal with the young man's family. Nobody had thought of that but her.

choices.text: Beg their pardon, and go

effects.log: You go off down the road, walking fast, with the hat on very straight. Behind you, you can hear him start again from the beginning. He is getting better at it. You would really rather not have noticed that.

events.text: A wine-seller on Bell Street tells you that this is the finest clear wine in the capital. "No," you say. It is watered by a third. You add where he gets the water. It has gone very quiet in the street. A good many people are looking into their cups. You are not sure what you have done, but you are now running.

choices.text: Run. Think about it later

effects.log: You go over two walls. It is your first experience of being chased, and you are not at all good at it. You get home to your stone at dawn, with your hat on crooked, and you stay very still, for the rest of the month.

choices.text: Stop, and turn round, and let them come

effects.log: It is not an impressive beating. They are mostly upset. You sit in the gutter with your nose running, and you explain to them, kindly, that the second cooper is also lying about the barrels. Somebody starts crying. It takes you a long while to find out why that was a mistake.

events.text: There is a small girl sitting on the steps at the drum, with a piece of rope. She has lost her dog. She tells you about it. She asks you, because of the hat, whether he is coming back. You can smell it on the rope: it has been some time, and you know what is done with dogs in a hungry year. Your mouth is opening. There is a thing that any person in this street could say to her.

choices.text: Say it. You have no other thing to say. Then stay with her

effects.log: "No," you say. Her face comes apart. You did not know that it could. You sit down on the step, with your hat in your hands, and you stay there until someone comes. It is a long time. You have never understood anything so well, or been able to do less about it.

choices.text: Shut your teeth on it, and walk away with your mouth full of leaves

effects.log: You walk until you are out of the city. It is not a lie. You have not said one thing. You look at that closely, for the whole of the winter, and you cannot find any flaw in it, and you do not feel at all clean.

events.text: {npc} sells radish soup from a cart at the east end of the gate. {He} asks everyone the same thing, not looking up, ladling. "How is the soup?" "Good," they all say, and each one rings a little flat. You take the bowl, and you drink some. "Thin," you say. "And you have charged me for radish." The ladle stops. The whole line goes silent. {He} looks up, and {he} has a very long, slow, delighted smile.

choices.text: Hand back the bowl, and wait for whatever comes next

effects.log: "Sit down," says {npc}, and {he} fills it up again. "Twenty years. Nobody. How is it now?" You drink. You tell {him}. {He} writes something on the side of the cart with a piece of charcoal. You have the impression you are being hired.

choices.text: Put down your coins, and go, and do not come back this way

effects.log: You find another way to the gate. It is a good deal longer. Nobody on that road ever asks you anything. A year or so later, the soup at the east end of the gate is said to have got rather worse, as though no one had been checking.

events.text: {npc} has discovered what you are good for. You are sat on a stool, behind the cart. Everyone comes. Is it true about the mill? Will the Lim boy pass the examination? You answer. No. No. Not all of it. By the second week, {he} has stopped asking you anything else, and you are not as pleased as you had expected to be.

choices.text: Ask {him} what {he} wants to know on {his} own account

effects.log: {He} stops with a question half out of {his} mouth. {He} has a look at you. "What do you mean?" {he} says. You mean what you said. You always do. It is a very quiet afternoon after that, and the soup boils over. {He} does not ask you about the mill again.

choices.text: Go on answering. It is what you came for

effects.log: You answer. The sister does not marry, and the Lim boy does not sit the examination, and the cousin moves to the provinces. You hear what they say about {npc} now. There is more dry wood under that street than you had counted, and you have been laying it.

events.text: {npc} is doing the accounts. "Am I handsome?" {he} says, out of nowhere, not looking up. "No," you say. {He} nods, and {he} moves a bean from one pile to the other. "Anything at all?" You look carefully. "Your ears are level," you say. "Most people's are not." {He} puts {his} chin on {his} hand. "Do you want to keep coming here?" "Yes." "Is that because of the soup?" "No."

choices.text: Say nothing further. It is {his} turn

effects.log: {He} goes back to the beans. {He} moves about four. {He} has gone a slow dark red, up to {his} level ears. "No one," {he} says, to the beans, "in all my life, has ever said anything to me that I could put any weight on." It is not a question, so you say nothing.

choices.text: Tell {him}, since it is true, that this frightens you

effects.log: "It frightens you?" says {npc}. You had not known that anything could. You tell {him} how much, and {he} asks you where in the body, and you tell {him} that too. {He} starts laughing. You note that this is a good sound, and {he} says, "Do not note it."

events.text: You had better say it. "There is one thing," you say. "You can ask me anything, for as long as we live. You will always get the answer. But there is one sentence that you must not ask me. It is, What are you?" {npc} looks at you, and at the hat. "Because you would say," {he} says. You would say. And then you would have to go.

choices.text: Say it plainly: you want to marry {him}, and that is the only condition

effects.log: {He} wipes {his} hands. "Tell me that you want to," {he} says. You tell {him}. {He} stands very still, as if {he} were hearing it from a long way off, and {he} says all right. Nobody in that street has ever been so sure of anything, and the soup is thin at the wedding.

choices.text: Say that nobody should have to live next to a thing like that

effects.log: "Is that true?" says {npc}. You open your mouth. It is. It seems to be. {He} looks at you, for a time, and then {he} goes back to ladling. "How is the soup?" {he} says, without looking up. You tell {him}. It is the last time.

events.text: Every morning {npc} sets a bowl in front of you, and folds {his} arms. "Well?" "Salty." {He} takes it away. Next day: "Well?" "Burnt." It has been six years. It is not an unhappy house. {He} has told the neighbours that you say that it is getting better. You have not. You do not bring this up.

choices.text: Show {him} where the radish goes wrong

effects.log: You stand by {him} for an entire morning, knowing nothing whatever about soup, and you tell {him} when it starts to taste false. It is a matter of when you add the salt. It is not much of a difference, and {he} throws a ladle at you.

effects.log: You eat every bite. It is a great deal of bad soup, in the end. {He} watches you do it, with {his} chin in {his} hand. "You are a very strange kind of person," {he} says. You open your mouth. {He} raises one finger, and {he} shakes it at you, and you shut it.

events.text: There are guests. {npc}'s aunt has brought a baby, and it looks like an old magistrate who has been told bad news. "Is that not the loveliest thing you ever saw?" the aunt says. Under the table, something hits your shin. "Ow," you say. They all look at you. "Why did you say ow?" the aunt says. You tell the aunt. {npc} has shut {his} eyes. The aunt says, slowly, "And what about the baby?"

effects.log: Everyone is holding their breath. It looks at you. It has got hold of your finger, and it is pulling very hard. "It is strong," you say, and it rings true as a bell. The aunt is satisfied. {npc} kicks you again, under the table, but this time rather gently.

choices.text: Tell the aunt

effects.log: It is a short description, and accurate. Nobody comes to the house for the whole of the next year. {npc} makes the soup, slamming things. You go out to the gate one evening, and you look at your own face on a hat, and you think that it could stand to be a good deal sorrier.

events.text: You wake in the night with the kitchen on fire, and {npc} is on the other side of it with a bucket. You walk in. You open your mouth, and you breathe, and it comes to you, all of it, and it goes down like hot broth. You turn around, with smoke coming out of your nose. {npc} is standing there. {His} mouth has opened, and you can see the first word in it.

choices.text: Stand still, and wait for it. You cannot do anything else

effects.log: It is the longest moment of your marriage. {He} shuts {his} mouth. {He} looks at the black beam, and at your face. {He} goes and fills a bowl with cold water, and {he} puts it in your hands. "You had it too hot," {he} says. "Blow on it, next time."

choices.text: Say, "The fire is out," quickly, and go and look at the thatch

effects.log: It is out. That is true. You are very busy with the thatch. {He} comes out after some time, and {he} holds the ladder. Neither of you says anything about it, and you have now both got something to not say. It is wonderful how much room it takes up.

events.text: {npc} has got a list. {He} would never ask it. But you will answer anything else, and over the mending, in an idle sort of voice, {he} has started to go around the edges. "Do you need to eat?" "Not much." "Have you got family?" "Not in the way you mean." "Do you feel the cold?" "No." "Are you older than the gate?" {He} is looking at {his} needle.

choices.text: Say it first. It is not a lie if nobody has to ask. "I am the stone before the gate"

effects.log: {He} sews to the end of the seam. {He} bites it off. "I know," {he} says. "I have been selling soup in front of you for twenty years. You have got moss in your left ear." So nobody has asked. You sit down on the floor, because your knees have gone, and that is not a thing that they usually do.

choices.text: Answer that one too. Go on answering, for as long as {he} goes around

effects.log: "Yes," you say. "Older than the gate." {He} nods, and {he} moves on to something else. It goes on, for years. It is the best game that either of you has ever played, and you both lie awake sometimes, thinking about how close it is.

choices.text: Take down your hat, tonight, and go. {He} is one question off

effects.log: You leave the hat on the peg, for you will not need it. You leave the door on the latch. It would be easy to say that you are going for a walk. You stand for a long time in the lane, with your mouth shut. There is nothing that you are able to call back.

events.text: You told the truth at the magistrate's, because they asked. It was {npc}'s own cousin. {He} stands in the door, with the soup going cold behind {him}. "Thirty years I have fed you," {he} says. "What is wrong with you? You could have said you did not recall. You have nothing in there. What ARE you?" It is only anger. Your mouth has already opened.

choices.text: Answer. It was asked

effects.log: You tell {him}. It takes four words. It is very quiet in the house, and you can hear the cart outside. {He} is looking at you, and {his} anger has gone out, and there is no knowing what is coming up behind it. You get your hat. {He} says, "Sit down. It was not a question. Sit down."

choices.text: Get a chinaberry leaf between your teeth, and bite until it stops

effects.log: It takes both hands. It is the hardest that you have ever bitten anything, and something in your forehead goes cold and gives a small tick. {He} has seen. You stand there, with your mouth full and your eyes running. "No," {he} says, after a long while. "Never mind. I withdraw it."

choices.text: Walk straight out, past {him}, before your mouth can finish

effects.log: You get as far as the lane, and you are saying it. It comes out of you anyway, four words, in the dark, to a dog. You go on walking. You never did learn what {he} did with the soup. You find out, some years later, that the cart has gone from the gate.

events.text: They hold up {bk_child} for you to see, and the midwife tells you it was an easy birth, and that makes you wince, and {npc} sees you do it. {He} is lying there grey and wet with {his} hair stuck to {his} face. Everyone in the room is waiting. "Well?" says {npc}, in hardly a voice at all. "How is it?" You look. It has a face like a boiled turnip. It has got one eye shut. You have been asked. The room is very hot.

choices.text: "Red. Creased. Loud. I would die for it. I had no idea"

effects.log: You hear it come out. That last bit was news to you. It rang very clear in the room, and the midwife has stopped with the cloth in one hand. {npc} starts to laugh, and it hurts, and {he} tells you to get out. {He} has never looked so well.

choices.text: "It looks like a turnip"

effects.log: That is all you can get out. {npc} holds out {his} hand for it. "You are a turnip," {he} says to the baby. "That is on the best authority." It gets to be the child's name around the house, for a good many years. They will not forgive you at the wedding.

events.text: A second one, {bk_child}, three years old now. There is a jar in pieces on the kitchen floor, and rice from wall to wall, and {bk_child} is standing in the middle, covered in it. "Who did this?" says {npc}. {bk_child} looks up with round eyes. "The cat," says {bk_child}. It goes right through your head, small and clear and perfect, the first one. Your own, and it can do the thing that you never could.

choices.text: Kneel down and say that you heard that. Say what a lie is

effects.log: You explain it. It takes a long time, with the rice. {bk_child} watches your mouth with great interest. "The cat," says {bk_child} again, to see what you will do. {npc} has had to go out into the yard. You can hear {him} from here.

choices.text: Look at it. Say nothing. You had not known that it could be so lovely

effects.log: It stays with you for days, that one clear wrong note. You have heard ten thousand, and you have hated all of them. {npc} looks at you. "You are grinning," {he} says. "It broke my jar." You would like to know how it is done, you tell {him}.

events.text: {bk_child} is seven, and everyone likes {bk_child}. Your neighbour's soup is very good, according to {bk_child}. The aunt's new baby is beautiful. The teacher is a clever man. You hear each of these go by, sour and small. {bk_child} gets asked to everything, and comes home with rice cakes. {bk_love} watches you hear it, across the table, and passes you the salt.

choices.text: Eat the rice cake, and mean it

effects.log: It is a very good one, and you say so. {bk_child} looks at you in surprise. It will be a long and pleasant life, and you are glad, and you say that too. It rings true, and it hurts a bit behind the eyes, and that is all.

choices.text: Ask {bk_child} what the soup at home is like

effects.log: {bk_child} looks at {bk_love}. Then looks at you, for some time, weighing it up. "It is very good," says {bk_child}, kindly. It is the flattest note you ever heard. You take it, and you put it away somewhere safe. You have not been told that before.

events.text: A fire in the lane, three roofs gone. You are running for it when you see {bk_child}, who is seven, standing in the road in a sleeping shift, mouth wide open, breathing in. The whole fire leans that way. It comes down the lane in a long red rope and goes in. And {bk_child} sits down, sooty and pleased. {bk_love} looks from that black small mouth to you. "Does it run in the family?" You are asked. "Yes," you say.

effects.log: {bk_child} would like some water, please, and says that it was hot. {bk_love} goes and gets it. Nobody asks the other thing, not then, and not after. You can hear the neighbours arriving, and each of them has a story ready. It is going to take a lot of chinaberry.

effects.log: You cannot, so you do not. You stand between them and the child, with your mouth shut, and let them make what they will of it. {bk_love} says it, about the wind, in a loud clear voice. It is a beautiful wrong note. You have never been so grateful for anything.

events.text: {npc} sets a bowl in front of you. {He} has to use both hands now. It has been forty-one years. You have told {him} thin, and salty, and burnt, and thin. {He} folds {his} arms. "Well?" You drink. You stop. You drink some more, for you must be sure. It has a clean sweet heat that goes straight down. You put the bowl down on the table. "It is good," you say.

choices.text: Say it again. {He} will want to hear it twice

effects.log: {He} does not move. Then {he} feels behind {him} for the stool, and {he} sits. "Say it again," {he} says. You say it. It rings like a temple bell, in that small kitchen. {He} puts {his} apron over {his} face. It is some time before {he} says, from under there, that {he} has no idea what {he} did.

choices.text: Add, because it is true, that the radish was very good this year

effects.log: There is a pause. "The radish," says {npc}. {He} looks at you for quite some time. Then {he} starts to wheeze, and {he} goes on wheezing, holding the table. You are worried. You ask {him}. "Forty-one years," {he} says, wiping {his} eyes, "and it is the radish."

events.text: {bk_love} is laid out at last, and the whole of the east gate has come. A wonderful cook, they say. So generous. Never a harsh word. You stand by the bier with your hat in your hands, and it goes by you, one after another, every note of it wrong, and you have hated that sound for all your life. Then they all stop, and they look at you. It is your turn.

choices.text: Say it. "The soup was thin for forty-one years. I had it every day."

effects.log: It rings all the way to the gate. Nobody breathes. Then an old woman begins to laugh, and she cries, and all of them do. It is the only thing that anyone there will remember. You go home. There is a bowl on the table, and you do not move it.

choices.text: Say nothing. Bow to them, for each of those wrong notes

effects.log: You bow. You had never thought of it. It was the only way that they had of saying it, and they were saying it as hard as they could, the whole lane, flat, with their faces wet. You have been standing at that gate a long time, and you have been a fool.

events.text: Some eighty years go by. A family in the south counties has lost another magistrate's post. It seems the man was shown a poem by the governor, and was asked. They are bad guests, and very good at law, and they cannot be got to say that anyone looks well. They make a thin radish soup. They will tell you so themselves.

choices.text: Keep the fire off that street

effects.log: There has been a good deal of fire in the south counties. It goes around them, one way or another. They do not seem to have noticed. They have been heard to say that the fire office is overpaid, and that it is badly run, which is true.

choices.text: Lay your ears back, on the plinth, as they go by

effects.log: One of them has brought a petition to the capital. {bk_child}'s people have the same walk, stiff in the neck. They come past you with their chin up, and they do not look, and you press your stone ears flat to your head. Only a small boy notices it, and nobody believes him.

events.text: After the night bell, someone comes and sits down on your plinth, and takes off a censor's hat. They have got {bk_child}'s level ears. They look worn out. They have an appointment in the morning, in front of everyone, with a very large person who has asked for one small word. It would save some forty people. They look up at your chin. "Just the once," they say. "Would it kill me?"

choices.text: Say nothing. You are a stone. Let them hear it

effects.log: You do not breathe. They sit there for a long time. In the morning they put on the hat, and they go in. You hear what they said, later on, and you hear what happened to them. They said the true thing. You do not know that you would have told them to.

choices.text: Let the bell at your throat ring, once, very low

effects.log: They jump, and they look at you, and they look at the hat. It tells them nothing, and that is the whole idea. You will never find out which it was that they said. It is the first thing about that family that you have not known, and you are surprised at how much better you feel.

events.text: {npc} sets up on your corner one morning, a very old peddler of dried fish and the most shameless liar that you have ever heard. {He} once wrestled the king's uncle. Each word goes through your head like a drunk falling down stairs. It is magnificent. {He} comes right over. "You," {he} says, "look thirty, and you are the handsomest person I ever saw."

choices.text: Say that {he} is lying, and that you would like to hear some more

effects.log: {He} is enchanted. {He} has never met anyone who could tell, and {he} has been at it for sixty years with no appreciation at all. You sit on an upturned basket. It is like a very bad court band, tuning up, for you alone. You tell {him} what you are, and {he} says that {he} knew it, which {he} did not.

choices.text: Buy one fish, and go back to your stone

effects.log: It is not from the Yellow River. You chew it on the plinth, in the dusk, and it is quite the saltiest thing that you have ever tasted. Your ears ache from the quiet. You can hear {him} from here, faintly, telling someone that {he} knows you.

events.text: A person has stopped in front of you, in the rain. "So it is you," they say. You know that note. "Nobody has asked me to a second wedding. I have lost four posts and a friend, and I told my own mother how she looked at the end. I have come a long way to say that I blame you." They wait. "And?" You are stone.

choices.text: Let your ears go flat, in the rain, in front of them

effects.log: It takes a long while for stone. They stand and watch it happen. They do not say anything for some time. "Well," they say, and their voice is not quite right. "Do not do that. People will think that I have done something." They go on, with their back very straight.

choices.text: Say it. "Was it worth it?" You would really like to know

effects.log: It comes out of your stone throat with a sound like a mill. They do not jump. They think it over with care, for they can do no other, and you can see them looking. "Ask me again when I am dead," they say. It rings quite true.

events.text: They say that it will not hurt. You are six, and the bonesetter has your arm, and something happens in your ears: a bad note, as from a cracked bell. You scream. It has nothing to do with your arm, which the bonesetter has not touched. {npc}, an old friend of the house, who is holding you still, looks at your face. "It will hurt a lot," says {npc}. You stop screaming.

choices.text: Hold still for the true one. It is much easier

effects.log: It hurts a lot. You had been told. You thank {npc}, in a shaky voice, and {he} looks rather thoughtful, and the bonesetter does not come back. From then on, you always ask {him} first, and it is a long time before you think to wonder why {he} answers.

choices.text: Put your fingers in your ears, until they stop saying things

effects.log: They think that you are simple, and that is very restful. You can keep your fingers in there for a whole dinner. You get a name for being a dreamy kind of child. You can still hear the worst ones, a little, through your teeth.

events.text: The village teacher is telling the Yun family that their boy is very promising. You are ten. You are carrying the ink. You look at the boy, and the boy looks at you, for the boy knows it too. "The boy is not," you say. You did not mean to. The boy's aunt is looking at you, and so is the teacher. It is a very long walk home, and {npc} has already heard, and {he} is sitting on your step.

choices.text: Say that it is true, and that you do not see the difficulty

effects.log: "No," says {npc}. "You would not." {He} shifts over. {He} explains to you about the Yun boy's fees, who pays them, and who eats if they do. You had not known any of that. You have still got it right. It is only that you now know what it weighs.

choices.text: Learn to bite your tongue. Do it literally, if you have to

effects.log: It is a useful trick. You have got a small hard place on the left side of your tongue by the time that you are twelve. You say that the Yun boy is doing well. It tastes like a leaf. People have started to say that you have improved.

events.text: There is an old chinaberry at the back of the mill, and you have been eating the leaves. You are fourteen. It is the most bitter thing in the province, and every other child who has tried it has been sick. You go up there after a bad day, and you sit and chew. Your head clears, like a room when someone has opened the door. {npc} finds you there, with your mouth green.

choices.text: Offer {him} a leaf

effects.log: {He} takes it, and {he} chews, and {his} whole face closes up. "No," {he} says, when {he} is able. {He} spits for some time. "Your people always did have it worst," {he} says, and {he} will not say any more, and you notice that it was a true thing, as far as it went.

choices.text: Say that it is for a stomach ache, and hate how it sounds

effects.log: It is the first lie that you have told out loud. It comes out like a cough. It is very ugly, and your own ears ring with it for two days. {npc} says, "I hope that it gets better," quite seriously. You give up the leaves for a while.

events.text: You are sixteen, stoking the ondol, and you look down, and your hand is in the fire. It is a little like holding a warm egg. There is something in your forehead that aches, as though a tooth wanted to come. You look up, and {npc} is in the door. {He} has seen. "Do not eat it," {he} says, tiredly. "They all want to eat it. Come and sit, and I will tell you about the hat."

choices.text: Sit, and hear about the hat

effects.log: One of the family sat the examination with a horn under a hat. A marriage, a sentence, a child called {bk_line}, and the stone before the gate, {bk_anc}. "It is all true," says {npc}. You know that it is. You have never in your life had anything explained to you that rang so well, or that you liked so little.

choices.text: Put it back, and say that you burned yourself

effects.log: It rings like a dropped pan. {npc} winces. So do you. You have no mark on your hand, and you bind it up, and you look at the cloth. "There will be time," {npc} says, on a clean note. "It does not go away. I am sorry."

events.text: You are not popular. You were at the Seo wedding, and the groom's uncle told a long story about a tiger, and you did not say anything. You only made a face. It is the face. It all sounds to you like somebody tuning a zither with a hammer. {npc} says that you might try going to fewer weddings, and {he} says that it is meant kindly, and it is.

choices.text: Go anyway. Sit by the door, and try to enjoy the food

effects.log: They do not throw you out. You eat a very great deal of rice cake, alone, and you are told that you are looking well, seven times. You get home with a headache. There is one old aunt who sits with you, because the old aunt is deaf.

choices.text: Stop making the face. Say the thing. They should at least know why

effects.log: You say the thing. The story is a very old one, you tell them, and the tiger was a dog. Nobody thanks you. But a few weeks later a stranger comes looking for you from two villages over. The stranger has got a will, and would like you to hear it read.

events.text: A merchant named Gwak has heard about you. You sit in the corner, in a good coat, and say nothing, while he buys ginseng. Every so often he looks over at you, and you scratch your nose, and he offers less. It goes well for a season. Then a seller comes in, an old farmer in a patched coat, and tells Gwak the price that his sick wife needs. It rings as true as a bell. Gwak looks over at you, for his cue.

choices.text: Scratch your nose, and tell him it is true. Do your job

effects.log: Gwak offers half, knowing now that the old man has no choice. You did only what you were paid for, and you told no lies. You get the good coat cleaned. You find that you cannot get that smell out of it, and {npc} has stopped laughing.

choices.text: Stand up, and tell the farmer what Gwak has just been told

effects.log: Gwak has you put out in the road, and the coat is Gwak's. The old farmer gets the price, from someone else, and never knows your name. {npc} finds you sitting there, and {he} has brought you your other shirt. "You are unemployable," {he} says, with satisfaction.

events.text: The family soup is thin. It is a family thing, the radish and how long you leave it. At the new year someone always says, "How is the soup?" and everyone at the table says, "Thin," and they all look pleased. The Yun in-laws are here this year, looking appalled. {npc}, at your elbow, wants to know if you would care to explain this to them.

choices.text: Tell them. From the beginning, with the cart at the gate

effects.log: It is a long story, and you are a poor storyteller, for you leave nothing out. They look at the bowl, and they look at you, and at the row of pleased faces. The youngest Yun picks up a spoon, tries it, and says, "Thin." So that is one more.

choices.text: Tell them that it is a family joke, and pass them the rice

effects.log: They laugh in relief, in thin high voices that hurt your teeth. You eat your soup. You know very well what it is that you did not tell them, and you would like to know who you got that from. It was somebody who kept their mouth shut, for a very long time, about one thing.

events.text: {npc} has had a new coat made, and {he} has come into the room in it, and {he} has turned around. {He} has been doing this for years. {He} never asks. {He} watches your face instead. Today {he} stops, with {his} back to you. "Just this once," {he} says. "Say something nice. Anything. I do not care if it is true."

choices.text: Tell {him} about the bad notes, and why you can never do it, and what it means when you say anything at all

effects.log: You tell {him}. {He} comes and sits down, in the coat. "So when you said, that first time, that you wanted me," {he} says. Yes. "And on the day of the fever?" Yes. "All of it? Every one?" It takes until the morning, for {he} has got a very long list. {He} has never been so happy.

choices.text: Try. Open your mouth, and say the coat is lovely

effects.log: It comes out like something being sick. You have a nosebleed. {He} turns around, and {he} looks at you, with the blood on your lip, and {his} eyes get very bright. "That is the nicest thing that anyone has ever done," {he} says. You cannot tell {him} that you agree. You have got no breath left.

events.text: {npc} has a split lip. {He} told the Ko boy something. {He} tells you what, furiously, and it was true, and it is the worst thing that you have heard all year. You know that face. You have seen it in the water all your life. {He} wants you to say that you are proud. You are not sure. And {he} would hear it.

choices.text: Sit {him} down. Teach {him} what you know about keeping quiet, and what it costs

effects.log: You teach {him} to bite the left side of {his} tongue. You tell {him} about the leaf. It is a long talk. "So I can say it, or not," {he} says, "but I can never say the other thing." That is right. {He} thinks it through. "That is really unfair," {he} says, and {he} is correct.

choices.text: Say, "It was true. It was also cruel." Then get the cloth for that lip

effects.log: {He} looks up. {He} has heard it ring both times. {He} lets you do the lip, and {he} does not say anything. It will be years before you hear from the Ko family on that matter. {He} goes back and apologises, you find out, and it is the worst apology in the history of the district.

events.text: {npc}, a soft-voiced official of some kind, sits next to you at the inn, and there is no bad note in {him}. None. {He} tells you that {he} serves a great house, that {he} has heard of a certain gift, and that {he} wishes you nothing but health. It rings clear, every word. {He} has ruined eleven families, you find out, and {he} has never said a false thing in {his} life.

choices.text: Do not listen. Take {him} by the collar, and put {him} in the road

ok.log: {He} sits in the mud, not at all put out, and {he} straightens {his} hat. "I shall tell my lord that you were quite well," {he} says. That is also true. You stand there, shaking, for you have never been frightened by the truth before.

fail.log: {He} is very quick, and {he} has done this a lot. You are on your back, with something in your ribs. "I have not told you that I would not," {he} says, and {he} steps over you. {He} really has not. You go back through all of it, and you find that {he} is right.

choices.text: Say as little as you can, and listen for what {he} leaves out

effects.log: You sit with {him} until the lamp goes down. It is the most interesting talk you have ever had. It is all in the gaps. You work out by the end that {he} has a list, and what your name is doing on it. "It was a pleasure," {he} says. It is.

events.text: {npc} is at your gate, grey now, and quite unchanged. "I have come to tell you what will happen," {he} says, and it rings clean. "My lord's faction wants a truth-drug for the trials. It is made from the bone of the horn, in your line. They will start with the youngest. I would prefer that it were you, and I can arrange that. I admire you," {he} says, and it is true.

choices.text: End it here, at the gate, with your hands

ok.log: You do not recall much of it. {He} does not call out. When it is over, {he} says, "Yes, I had thought that you might," and it rings as clear as anything. It is a good thing to have your hands shake, you think. It is the only thing about this that seems right.

fail.log: You are not as quick as a person who has planned this for twenty years. You lie in your own gate, and {he} bows. "I told you," {he} says, and {he} leaves. You have until the new moon, it seems, and everyone who knows you will know why you are limping.

choices.text: Go to the drum, with {him} at your heels. Beat it. Ask {him}, in front of everyone

effects.log: You make {him} say it. You ask {him}, in plain words, what {he} has done. {He} could stay silent. {He} looks at you, and {he} seems almost relieved. {He} speaks for about an hour, on a very clear note, and they have to send for more clerks.

events.text: You wake in the dark, with your feet cold, at the petition drum, with the stick in your hand. It is a long way from your bed. You do not know what it was that you came to say. You know that there is a great deal of it. {npc} is sitting on the steps.

choices.text: Beat it. You will think of what to say

effects.log: It is a very loud noise, in the quiet. Lamps come on, all along Bell Street. It turns out that you have a lot to say, about grain, and about one clerk's cousin. You lose your post by midday. {npc} says that {he} would have liked to get to bed first.

choices.text: Put back the stick. Go home, and take a little something to help you sleep

effects.log: You go home. You say to your neighbour, at the well, what a fine morning it is. It tastes like a leaf, and you swallow it. You have the sleeping draught every night from then on. You wake up in your bed, and it is very quiet, and your teeth hurt.

events.text: You smell smoke the whole time now. Nobody else can. It is a dry year, and you can see the fire mountain in the south. You can see the rest of it, too: every lie in this town, laid under the roofs like kindling, stacked very neatly, house after house, and some of them are yours. Somebody will have to stand somewhere and look at that mountain. {npc} has brought you a leaf.

choices.text: Go and stand at the south gate. Say what you know, street by street

effects.log: You stand for nine days. You name it all. You have been hit with a good many things, by the end of it, and you have lost every friend that you had left. But nothing burns that year in this town, or not much. It rains on the tenth day, and you are hoarse.

choices.text: Move out to the country. There is less to hear out there

effects.log: It is very peaceful among the cabbages. They tell you little, and it is all true. You hear about it in the autumn, from a peddler. It was the whole of the south quarter. The peddler says that no one could have known, and it sounds to you like somebody dropping a pan.

events.text: {npc} takes you up to the gate, on a night of thin rain, when the guards are under the eaves. It is only a stone, with moss on its left ear. It is sitting up very straight. You stand in front of {bk_anc}. {npc} has taken off {his} hat. You know the one thing that nobody has ever said to it.

choices.text: Ask it. "What are you?"

effects.log: Nothing moves. You stand there until your coat is soaked. Then it speaks. It has a voice like a millstone, and it has been waiting a very long time. It tells you what it is. It is true, and it is short. Then it asks you the same.

choices.text: Say to its face that you are glad to see it, and see what it does

effects.log: You are not. It comes out flat, and there is no one to hear it but the two of you. The stone horn dips by the width of a hair, and you feel it in the bone of your head. Then the stone ears go back. So it knows why you said it. You laugh out loud in the rain.

events.text: You have brought a jar, and you feel a fool. You made the soup yourself, as you were taught. {npc} holds the lamp. You kneel and pour it out, into the hollow by the stone's left foot, worn there by something. There is a long silence. It is very late. And then {bk_anc} says, from a long way up, in that terrible voice: "Well?"

choices.text: Tell it the truth. "Thin"

effects.log: There is a sound. It starts somewhere under the road. Slates shake on the guardhouse. It takes you some time to understand that it is laughing, and that it has not done so for a very long time. All the way home, {npc} keeps asking you what it said, and you tell {him}.

choices.text: Say, "I made it for you. It is the best that I can do"

effects.log: It rings. The stone says nothing for so long that you get up to go. Then, very slowly, its ears go back, and they lie flat. It has only ever done that for the upright, they say. You had always thought that it would feel more like winning.

events.text: It is all noise now, and your forehead aches, and last week you ate the fire in the neighbour's stove while they were cooking on it. {npc} sits with you under the chinaberry. "Half of it will kill you," {he} says, truthfully. You could have the horn taken down: they know how. You could go and sit at the gate, and be stone. {He} hesitates. There is a third way, but you would have to keep your hat on.

choices.text: Have it filed down. Learn to say the soup is good

effects.log: It takes one afternoon, and you bite a strap. When it stops, the room is silent. Someone says that you are looking well. You listen to it. It is just some words. You turn round, with tears on your face. "So are you," you say, and it is not true, and nothing happens.

choices.text: Go and sit at the gate. Let your ears go back for whoever earns it

effects.log: You walk up to the gate, at dawn, and you sit down by the other one. There is room. It does not look at you. The cold comes up from your feet, quite slowly, and you stop having to say anything, ever again. It is the greatest relief that you have ever known.

choices.text: Keep the hat on. Go on hearing it, and go on going home

effects.log: Nobody could stand that for a lifetime. {npc} points out that somebody once did it for forty-one years, with soup, and that it does seem to be a matter of having something to go home to and complain about.

events.text: You have told your first one, to the fish seller. "That looks fresh," you said. Nothing happened. You went round all day after that, telling people things. You told {npc} that {he} was looking younger. You have told the Yun baby it was beautiful, and they let you hold it. You are invited to the Seo wedding.

choices.text: Go to the wedding. Tell the uncle that you love the tiger story

effects.log: The uncle tells it to you twice. You nod, and you laugh in the right places. You have got no idea at all whether anybody there likes you, and you never will again. They all say that they do. You have a wonderful time, and on the way home you feel a little cold.

choices.text: Try to keep it to one a day, on the small things

effects.log: It is harder than you would think. You find that you have got an eye for where it does the most good. A sick neighbour hears that the colour is back. You are quite an artist, within a month, and people cry when you come to see them.

events.text: People come and rub your nose for luck. There are some who tell you things. They come in the evenings, and they say what they have done. You have got all of the city now, in order. {npc} comes up on the first of the month, and {he} sets a bowl down by your left foot. {He} does not say that it is good. It steams in the cold.

choices.text: Lay your ears back, when somebody has earned it

effects.log: It is not very often. A water carrier, and an old clerk who told the truth about the grain, and once a child. Nobody ever sees you do it. They only feel, as they go by, that they have stood up a bit straighter, for no reason that they know of.

choices.text: Hold the fire off the south road, in the dry years

effects.log: It comes up over the mountain as it always has. You look at it. It looks at you. It is the only other thing in the country that has never told anyone anything. You have both got very used to one another, and the roofs stay on.

events.text: You have a post in the third-grade records, because no one will have you in anything higher. Nobody asks you to lunch. In the dry months you go out at night, and you eat the worst of it, and you come home with a sooty mouth, and {npc} hands you some water, not looking up. There is a very short list of people who do not lie to you, and it is restful.

choices.text: Sit at the drum one day a month, for whoever cannot pay

effects.log: It is a long line. Some of them are telling the truth. You can get quite fond of it, as you do of a bad tooth. They bring you radishes. There are some in the capital who have started to say that the third-grade records are the most dangerous place in the country.

choices.text: Go home for lunch

effects.log: It is a very ordinary lunch. You and {npc} say almost nothing. You can hear, from here, the whole of the capital going about its business, in every key there is, and you can hear {him} chewing. You would not care to change it.

events.text: You are old, and people have stopped asking your opinion. But the small ones have found you out. "How do I look in this?" You look. "Like a small child in an old coat." They scream with joy, and they run to get the others. {npc} tells you that they are lined up at the door. "Is this a good drawing?" "No." "Do I have a big head?" "Yes." "Do you like me?"

choices.text: Answer it. They know that you can only answer it

effects.log: "Yes," you say. It rings out. The small one stands quite still for a moment, as if someone had just hung something heavy around its neck. Then it goes off, walking very carefully. You have got about ten more of them to get through before dinner.

choices.text: Tell them to go and ask someone who will say something nice

effects.log: They give you a look of pure contempt. Nice is all they ever get. You tell them that one day they will be very glad of it. It is true, and you can see them hearing it, and it does no good whatever. They would like to know if you are going to die.

events.text: It is the last of the autumn, and they have got you propped up on the warm part of the floor. They have all been coming in, one by one. {npc} comes last, and {he} sits with you for a while. {He} takes your hand. {He} leans down. "You are looking so much better today," {he} says. It goes through your head like a bell falling down a well.

choices.text: Say it back, or try. "So are you."

effects.log: Well, you try. Nothing comes. You have got only breath for it, and no voice. {He} sees you trying, and {he} knows what it is. {He} starts to shake, and you do not know if that is laughing. You lie there holding on, and you listen to that wrong note go on ringing, as long as you can.

choices.text: Take it. Say nothing. It is the best one you have ever heard

effects.log: You have heard it all your life. You have heard ten thousand of them, and you could tell them all apart, and you have never told anyone that this was how it sounded: like somebody holding out both hands. You shut your eyes, so as to hear it better.
